title: Farting (flatulence)
meta_description: Flatulence is passing gas from the digestive system out of the back passage. It's more commonly known as "passing wind", or "farting".

structured_data_json_ld.description: Flatulence is passing gas from the digestive system out of the back passage. It's more commonly known as "passing wind", or "farting".

hasPart.description: It's normal to fart several times a day. It's only a problem if you notice a change, such as farting more than usual, or it's affecting your life.

hasPart.text:
Farting is usually nothing to worry about. Everyone farts, some people more than others.

What's normal is different for everyone. If you notice a change or it's affecting your life, there are things you can do.

hasPart.headline: What is normal farting?

hasPart.description: If farting is a problem for you, it can help to eat smaller meals, chew food slowly and avoid food that makes you fart, such as cabbage or onions.

hasPart.headline: Do
hasPart.text:
• eat smaller meals, more often

  • drink or chew food slowly, with your mouth closed

  • exercise regularly to improve how your body digests food

  • drink peppermint tea

hasPart.headline: Don't
hasPart.text:
• do not eat too many foods that are difficult to digest and make you fart

  • do not drink too much beer, wine or fruit juice

  • do not smoke or chew gum

hasPart.headline: Food and drinks that can make you fart
hasPart.text:
• cabbage
  • broccoli
  • cauliflower
  • brussels sprouts
  • pulses, like beans or lentils
  • dried fruit, like raisins or apricots
  • onions
  • food or drinks containing the sweetener sorbitol
  • fizzy drinks and beer

hasPart.headline: A pharmacist can help with excessive or smelly farts
hasPart.text:
Speak to a pharmacist about excessive or smelly farts.

They might be able to tell you:

  • if you can buy something to help – for example, medicines such as simeticone or special underwear and pads that absorb smells
  • if you should see a GP

hasPart.headline: Things you can do to reduce excessive or smelly farts
See a GP if:
hasPart.text:
• farting is affecting your life and self-help and pharmacy treatments have not worked
  • you have a stomach ache or bloating that will not go away or comes back
  • you keep getting constipation or diarrhoea
  • you have lost weight without trying
  • you've had blood in your poo

hasPart.description: Farting is often due to swallowing air or eating food that is hard to digest. It can also be caused by medicines or conditions like coeliac disease.

hasPart.text:
Excessive or smelly farts can be caused when you swallow air or eat foods that are difficult to digest. It can also sometimes be a sign of a health condition.

Do not self-diagnose. See a GP if you're worried about your farting.

Excessive or smelly wind can also be a side effect of some medicines, including:

  • non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS), like ibuprofen
  • some laxatives
  • antifungal medicines
  • statins

Do not stop or change your medicine without speaking to a GP first.

hasPart.headline: What causes excessive or smelly farts

hasPart.description: Farting, also known as flatulence or wind, is normal. There are things you can do if you fart a lot or they're smelly.

hasPart.text: Farting is often due to swallowing air or eating food that is hard to digest. It can also be caused by medicines or conditions like coeliac disease.
It's normal to fart several times a day. It's only a problem if you notice a change, such as farting more than usual, or it's affecting your life.
If farting is a problem for you, it can help to eat smaller meals, chew food slowly and avoid food that makes you fart, such as cabbage or onions.
